stage1.impression: A red-topped slab floating against vertical timber boards, with a wall lever tap and a dark bottle. It reads as CG. The boards are a smooth, evenly repeated procedural grain with no gaps or depth. The trough's front and side are a near-black box, so nothing glows through the acrylic, and it looks like glossy red paint on a black block rather than thick cast acrylic. The tap reads as a dark door handle, not brushed steel. A design magazine would not publish this as a specific place: it is a generic bathroom-vanity render with no sign of the bar around it.

blocking_9: The trough's front face and polished edges must visibly glow red through the thickness of the acrylic (front face [150,300,540,400] lum_median >= 25 with r_median >= 50), not read as an opaque black box
The timber boards must read as real boards at 1:1: shadow gaps between boards, tone varying from board to board, natural grain scale, no visibly repeated texture
The spout must read as brushed steel with a soft linear highlight, not a dark brown door lever
No region larger than a tenth of the frame more than half crushed (left strip [0,0,100,480] is 85 % crushed over 13.9 % of the frame)
Some sign of life and some room context so it reads as this bar's washroom, not a catalogue vanity (towel, soap, water, a sliver of the room)
The basin's interior must hold detail instead of reading as a black hole

defects.what: Trough front face is near black (lum_median 2.1, crush 68 %); no light through the acrylic's thickness, and the top-front polished edge does not glow
Basin interior is crushed black (median 2.3, crush 57 %); the soft rounded bowl reads as a sharp dark elliptical cut-out
Wall boards: uniform widths, no shadow gaps, flat CG wood grain with a repetitive figure; the tone is lilac-pink rather than warm timber
The under-glow lights the wall below (median 63) far more than the acrylic it should come through; it reads as an LED strip under a black box
The spout is dark brown with red reflections and a thin wire-like drop; it reads as a door lever, not brushed steel, and sits far above the basin
Dead black strip down the left (median 1.1, crush 85 %, 13.9 % of the frame) with no information
The bottle is an anonymous dark silhouette (median 4.3) with no glass highlight or label
Top surface: flat, uniform red gloss with soft smeared reflections; no thickness, depth or caustic glow, so it reads like paint or plastic

changes.problem: The acrylic trough does not glow through its thickness: its front face is black, so the hero object reads as a black box with a red lid.

change.setting: the sink's under-glow (emission strength), and the sink spot
change.from: under-glow 2.5; sink spot 18.0 W, 2700 K, cone 30 deg
change.to: under-glow 6.0, placed inside or against the underside of the acrylic so it couples into the slab; sink spot 30 W, 2700 K, cone 40 deg, aimed to graze the front face and top edge

changes.expected: The front face and the polished edges read as deep, saturated ember red with a gradient that is brighter toward the lit underside; the top-front edge shows a thin glowing line

changes.problem: The timber boards read as a smooth, repeated CG texture with no joints, so the whole frame says render.

evidence.measured: lum_range 40.1, lum_p5 29.8: no dark joints; same grain figure board after board at 1:1

change.setting: the timber boards' finish (the oak's stain)
change.from: one uniform procedural grain, boards flush and without gaps, pinkish tone
change.to: 4 mm shadow gaps between boards, per-board tone and hue offset of about ±10 %, randomised grain offset and rotation for each board, roughness 0.55 to 0.7 varying by board, stain shifted to warm dark brown (less magenta)

changes.expected: Distinct individual boards with dark joints and varied grain; the wall reads as real timber in warm brown

changes.problem: The under-glow's spill makes the wall below the brightest surface in the frame and pulls the eye away from the acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 63.2, while the trough's front face is 2.1

change.setting: the sink's under-glow direction and spread
change.from: a wide wash onto the boards below
change.to: keep the emitter but shield or angle it so most of its light goes into the acrylic; the wall below receives a soft pool that falls off within about 300 mm

changes.expected: The wall below sits below the trough's face in brightness, and the pool falls off downward

changes.problem: The spout reads as a dark brown door lever, not brushed steel.

evidence.measured: a dark brown body with a thin highlight only, tinted red; no anisotropic streak

change.to: brushed stainless: base colour about #8A8A88, metallic 1, roughness 0.3, anisotropy 0.6 along the spout's length

changes.expected: A clean linear highlight along the spout and handle, a neutral grey that is clearly steel

changes.problem: A dead black strip covers the left 14 % of the frame and carries no information.

change.to: pan right about 4 deg (target y 0.3 -> about 0.15) so the alcove's dark return leaves the frame, or keep the framing and let a sliver of the lit room show at that edge instead of black

changes.expected: No large crushed region; the trough fills the frame more fully and centrally

changes.problem: Nothing says anyone uses this sink or that it belongs to a bar: the basin is a black void and the only prop is an anonymous bottle.

change.to: an amber glass soap bottle (so it catches the sink's light), a folded linen hand towel on the deck, a few water droplets in the basin, a small rocks glass left on the deck

changes.expected: Small highlights on the deck and in the basin; the bowl's curve is readable; the frame reads as lived in

changes.problem: The top surface is a flat, uniform red gloss with no sense of depth, so it reads like paint or plastic.

evidence.measured: lum_range 40.7 on the lit deck; reflections soft and smeared

change.to: angle the spot so its specular reflection lands as one crisp hotspot on the deck behind the basin, and add a small candle on the deck (2 W, 1900 K) for a reflected point

changes.expected: One or two crisp, undistorted reflections on the deck, which read as polished thick acrylic

changes.problem: The overall grade turns the timber lilac-pink and leaves the frame flat, with no deep blacks apart from the dead strip.

evidence.measured: r 75, g 46, b 33 with low chroma that reads as pink-grey; frame p95 only 88

change.to: white_balance_k 2800 with a slight green-yellow tint (+0.05) toward warm brown; AgX look 'Medium High Contrast'

changes.expected: Warm brown timber and more contrast between the glowing acrylic and the wall; frame median stays in the 22 to 50 band

out_of_scope.request: Make the basin a soft, rounded hollow that blends into the top, as the card describes, rather than a sharp elliptical cut-out
out_of_scope.why: The sink's geometry is fixed by the room's design

out_of_scope.request: Lower the spout so it sits closer over the basin, and give it a more substantial body than a thin wire drop
out_of_scope.why: The spout is part of the sink as designed; its form and position are fixed

out_of_scope.request: Check that the acrylic's material actually transmits light (volume absorption sized to the slab's thickness) rather than rendering opaque
out_of_scope.why: The acrylic's tint and make-up are part of the sink's fixed design; if c1 fails, the material model is at fault, not the light
